rootSeed.description: Sole source of true randomness for the entire run; everything else is derived deterministically from this via SeedTree.

maxParallelism.description: How many threads generation may use. 1 (default) = one thread. 0 = every core. The result is identical whatever the number: threads only try quality retries of a plain/base glyph ahead of time, and the first attempt that passes in attempt order is the one kept.

angles.description: Angles the arc may start (and end) at. Default Cardinal. Only used when `anchor` is None or Node.

enumDescriptions: The arc starts at any angle of the preset, so it need not touch the current node (the original behaviour).

One end of the arc is the current node: it either starts there or ends there (either way round), and the sweep is drawn from minSweep..maxSweep. The sweep goes in steps of 90 degrees (45 when angles is Both); the preset's angles themselves are not used. The far node is still where the chain carries on from.
A half circle between the current node and the far node, bulging to either side. minSweep, maxSweep and the angles are not used. The arc always connects the two nodes.

anchor.description: Whether the arc has to touch the current node (see the values of `anchor`). Default None.

enumDescriptions: From the far end of the circle's diameter (the node 'length' steps away). With anchor Node that node need not lie on the arc. This is the default.

From the node the arc itself ends at (the nearest lattice node to its free end, within endTolerance). Needs anchor Node: the arc starts or ends on the current node, so the chain really continues along the arc. Arcs whose end is not close enough to a node are not offered.
markdownEnumDescriptions: From the far end of the circle's diameter (the node 'length' steps away). With anchor Node that node need not lie on the arc. This is the default.

From the node the arc itself ends at (the nearest lattice node to its free end, within endTolerance). Needs anchor Node: the arc starts or ends on the current node, so the chain really continues along the arc. Arcs whose end is not close enough to a node are not offered.
continueFrom.description: Where the chain carries on after the arc (see the values). Needs anchor Node. Default FarNode. Only used when `anchor` is Node.

endTolerance.description: continueFrom ArcEnd: how far (lattice units) the arc's end may be from the node the chain continues from. 0 = the arc must end exactly on a node. A larger value admits more arcs; the next stroke then starts from the node, up to this far from where the arc stops. Default 0. Only used when `continueFrom` is ArcEnd.

minSweep.description: Smallest sweep in degrees (a multiple of the preset's step: 90, or 45 for Both). 180 = a half circle. Default 90. Only used when `anchor` is None or Node.

maxSweep.description: Largest sweep in degrees, below 360. Default 270. Only used when `anchor` is None or Node.

ArcConfig.description: direction Arc: which part of the circle is drawn. The circle is set like a Circle rule's (its diameter runs from the current node to the node 'length' steps away); the arc starts at an angle of the preset, sweeps clockwise by a multiple of the preset's step, and so also ends on an angle of the preset.

crossing.description: Whether and where this shape's edges may cross edges already placed (curves count: a curved edge is checked as the curve it is drawn as). A crossing needs both shapes to accept it - the one being placed and the one that owns the edge it would cross - each by its own crossing settings.

spacing.description: Distances to keep from the shapes already placed (centroid and closest-node minimums/maximums). The rules of the shape being placed are checked against everything already there, so the outcome depends on placement order.

bias.description: Preference among placements that already satisfy every hard rule (grid bounds, crossing, spacing). Never relaxes a rule. Empty modes = no bias.

candidates.description: Shapes only: how many valid candidates to generate when a bias is active; the one whose glyph bounding box scores best is kept ("best of N"). Ignored without a bias, and by combination components (they search every placement exhaustively).

ArrangementRules.description: How a shape relates to the shapes already placed in the glyph: whether it may cross them, how far from them it must (or must not) sit, and which of several legal placements is preferred. Used by every entry in a language's shapes list and by the combination block (for the components of a composite).

enumDescriptions: Every step-th coordinate, starting at offset (step 3, offset 1: 1, 4, 7, ...).
Odd coordinates (1, 3, 5, ...).
Even coordinates (0, 2, 4, ...).
markdownEnumDescriptions: Every step-th coordinate, starting at offset (step 3, offset 1: 1, 4, 7, ...).
Odd coordinates (1, 3, 5, ...).
Even coordinates (0, 2, 4, ...).
mode.description: Which coordinates match: Every (every step-th, from offset), Odd or Even.

step.description: Every: the spacing between matching coordinates (1 = all). Default 1. Only used when `mode` is Every.

offset.description: Every: the first matching coordinate (counted from 0; 1 with step 3 = 1, 4, 7, ...). Default 0. Only used when `mode` is Every.

AxisPattern.description: Which values of one coordinate (x or y) match.

enumDescriptions: Width runs from the full width to a thin tip (tipWidth, taperSharpness).
A flat nib held at a fixed angle: thick and thin strokes by direction (nib* options).
Pressure and ragged edges like ink on paper (pressureVariation, edgeWobble, raggedness, startBlobScale).
markdownEnumDescriptions: Width runs from the full width to a thin tip (tipWidth, taperSharpness).
A flat nib held at a fixed angle: thick and thin strokes by direction (nib* options).
Pressure and ragged edges like ink on paper (pressureVariation, edgeWobble, raggedness, startBlobScale).
mode.description: The pen: Taper (full width narrowing to a tip), BroadNib (a flat nib at an angle) or Ink (pressure and ragged edges).

width.description: Maximum stroke width (Taper/Ink) or nib length (BroadNib).

taperSharpness.description: >1 = pointier, <1 = fuller. Only used when `mode` is Taper.

nibRoundness.description: 0 = a flat, square-ended nib; 1 = fully rounded ends (a capsule, like a brush pen). In between rounds the corners. Only used when `mode` is BroadNib.

nibAngleWobble.description: How far (degrees, +-) the hand lets the nib angle drift along a stroke, slowly and seeded per stroke. Only used when `mode` is BroadNib.

nibPressure.description: 0-1: how much the nib length (pressure) varies along a stroke. Only used when `mode` is BroadNib.

nibLeadIn.description: 0-0.5: fraction of an open stroke's length, at each end, over which the nib eases in from a light touch to full length, like a hand setting the pen down and lifting it. Only used when `mode` is BroadNib.

startBlobScale.description: >1 adds a blob where each stroke starts. Only used when `mode` is Ink.

BrushTypefaceConfig.description: Pen-like strokes. The mode picks the pen (Taper, BroadNib or Ink); each mode has its own options.

sizePx.description: Width and height in pixels of each rendered glyph image. Default 512 (at least 16).

marginPx.description: Empty border in pixels kept around the drawing inside the image. Default 32.

CanvasConfig.description: The size of each rendered glyph image and the empty border around the drawing.

length.description: How many nodes the chain should have (including the start node).

connectionRules.description: Weighted connection rules driving the chain's growth at each step. At least one is required, otherwise no chain can grow. A rule's `backToStartChance` above 0 needs `allowClosedLoop` to be true.

enumDescriptions: Every concrete move (each direction x length a rule allows) carries the rule's full Weight, so a rule with many valid moves ends up with more total probability than a narrow one of equal Weight. The original behaviour.

A rule's Weight is split evenly across its valid moves at each step, so the rule's total probability is Weight relative to the other rules' Weights, however many moves each has (a rule with no valid move at that step simply drops out).
markdownEnumDescriptions: Every concrete move (each direction x length a rule allows) carries the rule's full Weight, so a rule with many valid moves ends up with more total probability than a narrow one of equal Weight. The original behaviour.

A rule's Weight is split evenly across its valid moves at each step, so the rule's total probability is Weight relative to the other rules' Weights, however many moves each has (a rule with no valid move at that step simply drops out).
connectionWeighting.description: How connection-rule weights turn into move probabilities. See `connectionWeighting`.

allowNodeRevisit.description: Whether the chain may revisit nodes already in it.

allowEdgeRevisit.description: Whether the chain may revisit edges already in it.

allowClosedLoop.description: Whether the chain may close into a loop back to its start node. How likely that is is set per rule (connectionRules[].backToStartChance).

selfSpacing.description: Node-to-node spacing rules inside this chain, all enforced together as each node is added, on top of the ordinary intersection check. Empty = none.

ChainRules.description: How ONE stroke (chain) grows: its length, the weighted connection rules, how those weights become probabilities, whether it may revisit nodes/edges or close into a loop, and the spacing between its own nodes. Used by every Generative shape - there is no language-wide copy, so two shapes can follow different rules (long strokes and short ticks, say) and nothing is inherited silently. Ignored for Literal shapes.

contact.description: Make the components of a composite touch: at least min shared nodes (junctions) and/or crossings between different components, with a chance per composite. null (default) = no requirement. If the components do not touch, the last placed one is moved to a position where they do, then the other movable ones are tried in turn; if no position works the attempt fails and a component is regenerated, as for any other placement failure. A component with a Fixed placement is not moved; a recipe whose components (after the first) all have Fixed placements is exempt from the requirement.

placements.description: Placement rules by component glyph ("*" = every component without a rule of its own). Components without a rule are placed as before.

crossing.description: Whether and where this shape's edges may cross edges already placed (curves count: a curved edge is checked as the curve it is drawn as). A crossing needs both shapes to accept it - the one being placed and the one that owns the edge it would cross - each by its own crossing settings.

spacing.description: Distances to keep from the shapes already placed (centroid and closest-node minimums/maximums). The rules of the shape being placed are checked against everything already there, so the outcome depends on placement order.

bias.description: Preference among placements that already satisfy every hard rule (grid bounds, crossing, spacing). Never relaxes a rule. Empty modes = no bias.

candidates.description: Shapes only: how many valid candidates to generate when a bias is active; the one whose glyph bounding box scores best is kept ("best of N"). Ignored without a bias, and by combination components (they search every placement exhaustively).

CombinationArrangementRules.description: The arrangement of a combination's components: everything a shape's arrangement has, plus per-component placement rules. Placing order is the recipe's order, and each component is checked against those placed before it, so list the components you fix first.

enumDescriptions: Prefer the combined glyph to be as tall as possible.
Prefer the combined glyph to be as short as possible.
Prefer the combined glyph to be as wide as possible.
Prefer the combined glyph to be as narrow as possible.
Width and height as close to equal as possible (by ratio, so it holds at any size).
markdownEnumDescriptions: Prefer the combined glyph to be as tall as possible.
Prefer the combined glyph to be as short as possible.
Prefer the combined glyph to be as wide as possible.
Prefer the combined glyph to be as narrow as possible.
Width and height as close to equal as possible (by ratio, so it holds at any size).

modes.description: Empty = no bias: the first legal placement found is used (original behaviour).

weights.description: Optional weight per listed mode (default 1 for any mode not mentioned), e.g. { "Tallest": 3, "Squarest": 1 } to care three times as much about height as about squareness. A mode's score is multiplied by its weight before the scores are added; only the ratios matter. Weights for modes that aren't in Modes are rejected, as is giving every listed mode weight 0.

includeScaleAndRotation.description: Combination only (a shape's candidates are not scaled or rotated). false: bias only picks among TRANSLATIONS, at the first scale/rotation that has any legal placement (the existing "translate first, scale/rotate only as a fallback" order is kept). true: every allowed scale/rotation is also in the running, so e.g. Tallest can pick a larger scale or a 90-degree turn - strongest effect, but it overrides the translate-first preference.

CombinationBiasConfig.description: A preference, never a requirement: the bias only chooses between placements that already satisfy every other constraint (grid bounds, no crossing, sub-symbol spacing, allowed scales/rotations). If only one placement is legal, that one is used whatever it does to the shape. Components are placed one after another, so with three or more components the bias is applied greedily - each is placed to best serve the shape of what is already there. Several modes can be active at once; they are blended with equal weight (each is scored on a 0..1 scale relative to the grid, then the scores are added). E.g. Shortest + Narrowest asks for the smallest overall box, Tallest + Narrowest for tall and thin, Tallest + Widest for the biggest, Squarest + Shortest for a compact square. Opposites (Tallest + Shortest, Widest + Narrowest) cancel out and are rejected by validation.

recipes.description: Key = composite glyph name, value = component glyph names to overlay. A glyph name may appear both as a standalone entry in the language's glyph list and as a component here. Each value is a list of component names, or an object with "components" and an optional per-recipe "arrangement".

allowScale.description: Whether a component may be scaled when it is placed in a composite. The ratios come from allowedScales. Default false.

allowedScales.description: Discrete ratios only (each an exact fraction such as 2/3): a shrinking ratio is only usable when every node of the component divides exactly, which a continuous range could not guarantee. Only used when `allowScale` is true.

allowRotate.description: Whether a component may be rotated when it is placed in a composite. The angles come from rotation.allowed. Default false.

maxRetriesPerRecipe.description: How many times a composite is retried (regenerating its least-used components first) before the run fails with a named error. Default 5.

arrangement.description: How a composite's components relate to each other: crossing (default: none - overlay composition is controlled stacking, they may only touch at shared nodes), spacing bias and per-component placement rules (placements). A recipe can override parts of it with its own "arrangement". Each placed component counts as one shape. Components search every translation exhaustively, so arrangement.candidates does not apply here.

CombinationConfig.description: Overlay-composition rules for combined glyphs (e.g. Anchorite-style stacking). A composite glyph's components are generated independently first, then translated (and optionally scaled/rotated) onto the composite's own grid. On placement failure, the least-used dependency (the least-used glyph) is regenerated first, escalating through the recipe's components up to `maxRetriesPerRecipe` before the run fails with a named error.

components.description: Glyph names of the components whose nodes count. Left out = every component placed so far.

shapes.description: Only the nodes of these shapes (ids from shapes) inside those components. Left out = all their nodes.

ComponentNodes.description: The nodes of components already placed in the composite (combination placements only).

glyph.description: The component's glyph name, or a list of names (the rule then applies to each of them). The rule applies wherever that glyph is a component of a recipe the arrangement covers (every instance, if a recipe lists it more than once).

enumDescriptions: Like Prefer, but the sides are drawn at random (see Pick) for each composite instead of listed. Whatever is drawn then acts exactly like a Prefer rule with those sides.
Among the placements that pass every hard rule, take the one nearest the chosen side(s).
Exactly one placement: the component as it is in its own glyph, moved by offset. No scaling, no rotation, no alternatives - if it does not fit, the recipe cannot be built.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Like Prefer, but the sides are drawn at random (see Pick) for each composite instead of listed. Whatever is drawn then acts exactly like a Prefer rule with those sides.
Among the placements that pass every hard rule, take the one nearest the chosen side(s).
Exactly one placement: the component as it is in its own glyph, moved by offset. No scaling, no rotation, no alternatives - if it does not fit, the recipe cannot be built.
mode.description: What the rule does: Prefer (pull towards the listed sides), SetRandom (draw the sides at random) or Fixed (an exact offset).

enumDescriptions: The left edge.
The right edge.
The top edge (smaller y).
The bottom edge (larger y).
The middle of the grid. Only a pull (a ranking of the legal placements), never a hard rule, so it puts no condition on where the other components sit. Cannot be combined with other sides.
markdownEnumDescriptions: The left edge.
The right edge.
The top edge (smaller y).
The bottom edge (larger y).
The middle of the grid. Only a pull (a ranking of the legal placements), never a hard rule, so it puts no condition on where the other components sit. Cannot be combined with other sides.

sides.description: Prefer only: one or two sides. Two means a corner, so [Top, Left] is the top left. Left with Right, or Top with Bottom, cancel out and are rejected. Only used when `mode` is Prefer.

enumDescriptions: One of the four sides.
Two sides, one horizontal and one vertical: a random corner.
Left or Right.
Top or Bottom.
markdownEnumDescriptions: One of the four sides.
Two sides, one horizontal and one vertical: a random corner.
Left or Right.
Top or Bottom.

pick.description: SetRandom only: what is drawn. Default Any. Only used when `mode` is SetRandom.

enumDescriptions: Once per language and glyph: the glyph gets the same drawn side in every composite it is part of (so Man/Human sits in the same place everywhere, and a reader can learn it). The draw is fixed by the root seed and does not change when a composite is retried.
Once per composite: each composite draws for itself, so the same glyph can sit on different sides in different composites (and on a different one after a quality retry).
markdownEnumDescriptions: Once per language and glyph: the glyph gets the same drawn side in every composite it is part of (so Man/Human sits in the same place everywhere, and a reader can learn it). The draw is fixed by the root seed and does not change when a composite is retried.
Once per composite: each composite draws for itself, so the same glyph can sit on different sides in different composites (and on a different one after a quality retry).

scope.description: SetRandom only: whether the draw is made once for the whole language (default) or again for every composite. Only used when `mode` is SetRandom.

offset.description: Fixed only: how far to move the component from where it sits in its own glyph, as { "x": 2, "y": 0 } or [2, 0]. Omitted = not moved at all (the plain overlay). Only used when `mode` is Fixed.

enumDescriptions: Nothing else is tried: the recipe attempt fails, and the component (or another one) is regenerated.

The component, as drawn, is tried at every other position on the grid first (same size and rotation, in a shuffled but deterministic order). Only when it fits nowhere does the recipe attempt fail and a component get regenerated.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Nothing else is tried: the recipe attempt fails, and the component (or another one) is regenerated.

The component, as drawn, is tried at every other position on the grid first (same size and rotation, in a shuffled but deterministic order). Only when it fits nowhere does the recipe attempt fail and a component get regenerated.
ifBlocked.description: Fixed only: what to do when the fixed position is blocked (crossing, spacing, off the grid). Default Regenerate, as before; Translate tries every other position first. Only used when `mode` is Fixed.

weight.description: Prefer and SetRandom: how strongly the side pull counts against the arrangement's bias, when both are active (default 1; 0 turns the pull off).

nodes.description: Prefer and SetRandom: a node mask the component's nodes must hit (which node, see anchor). Same regions as a shape's placement.nodes (points, box, pattern) plus nodesOfComponents: nodes of components placed earlier, optionally only those of some shapes inside them. Only components placed before this one exist, so give the others a Fixed placement or put them earlier in the recipe. Only used when `mode` is Prefer or SetRandom.

enumDescriptions: The very first node of the component on the mask; if no placement is found, any node on the mask.
The very first node of the component (first node of its first stroke) on the mask, no fallback.
At least one node of the component, any, on the mask.
markdownEnumDescriptions: The very first node of the component on the mask; if no placement is found, any node on the mask.
The very first node of the component (first node of its first stroke) on the mask, no fallback.
At least one node of the component, any, on the mask.
anchor.description: With nodes: FirstThenAny (default) requires the very first node of the component (first node of its first stroke) on the mask and, only if no placement is found that way, accepts any node of it; FirstNode never falls back; AnyNode accepts any node from the start. Only used when `mode` is Prefer or SetRandom.

ComponentPlacementRule.description: Controls where one component (named by its glyph, or "*" for all of them) goes inside a composite.

enumDescriptions: The 4 straight directions (up, down, left, right).
The 4 diagonals.
All 8 of the above.

Any lattice node, at any angle. Length is the Chebyshev distance max(|dx|, |dy|), so length 1 is the same 8 neighbours as Both and longer lengths add the knight-move-style jumps in between. Combine with minAngle/maxAngle/anglePreset to limit the turn.
Like Any, but meant to be limited by an angle: needs minAngle/maxAngle or an anglePreset.

Draws a circle instead of a line. From the current node the circle runs to the node 'length' steps away in one of the 8 directions, and that pair of points is its DIAMETER; the chain then carries on from the far node. A diagonal circle of length L has diameter L*sqrt(2). minLength may be 0: length 0 is a dot on the current node (no circle, the chain continues from the same node). Angle limits do not apply.

Draws part of a circle: the circle is set like a Circle's (diameter from the current node to the node 'length' steps away, minLength at least 1) but only an arc of it is drawn, picked at random from the 'arc' settings. The chain carries on from the far node, which the drawn arc may or may not reach. Angle limits do not apply.

Like Any, but meant to be limited by an angle: needs minAngle/maxAngle or an anglePreset.

From the current node the circle runs to the node 'length' steps away in one of the 8 directions, and that pair of points is its DIAMETER; the chain then carries on from the far node. A diagonal circle of length L has diameter L*sqrt(2). minLength may be 0: length 0 is a dot on the current node (no circle, the chain continues from the same node). Angle limits do not apply.

direction.description: The kind of move this rule makes: a line (Orthogonal, Diagonal, Both, Any, Angle), a Circle, or an Arc.

minLength.description: Shortest move, in lattice units (1 = the neighbouring node). For a Circle it is the diameter, where 0 is a dot. Default 1.

maxLength.description: Longest move, in lattice units (for a Circle, the diameter). Must not be below minLength. Default 1.

weight.description: How likely this rule is to be picked relative to the chain's other rules (see chain.connectionWeighting). 0 = never. Default 1.

minAngle.description: Smallest allowed turn, in degrees, measured between the previous edge and the new one at the current node: 180 = carry straight on, 90 = right angle, 0 = fold back. The first edge of a stroke has nothing to turn from, so it is not limited. Applies to every direction except Circle. Only used when `direction` is Orthogonal, Diagonal, Both, Any or Angle. One of `minAngle`, `maxAngle`, `anglePreset` is required when `direction` is Angle.

maxAngle.description: Largest allowed turn, in degrees (see `minAngle`). Only used when `direction` is Orthogonal, Diagonal, Both, Any or Angle. One of `minAngle`, `maxAngle`, `anglePreset` is required when `direction` is Angle.

enumDescriptions: No preset: minAngle/maxAngle are used.
Carry on in a line: 170-180.
A gentle bend: 120-170.
About a right angle: 80-100.
A sharp turn back on itself: 0-60.
markdownEnumDescriptions: No preset: minAngle/maxAngle are used.
Carry on in a line: 170-180.
A gentle bend: 120-170.
About a right angle: 80-100.
A sharp turn back on itself: 0-60.
anglePreset.description: Shortcut for a minAngle/maxAngle pair; when set, it replaces them. Only used when `direction` is Orthogonal, Diagonal, Both, Any or Angle. One of `minAngle`, `maxAngle`, `anglePreset` is required when `direction` is Angle.

backToStartChance.description: Chance (0-100), each time this rule is the one picked, that the stroke instead goes back to its starting node and closes into a loop. Needs chain.allowClosedLoop and at least 3 nodes so far, and the closing edge must be free of crossings, otherwise the rule just makes its normal move. Replaces chain.closedLoopWeight.

chainLengthCost.description: How much of the chain's length this rule uses up each time it is drawn (default 1, which is one node, as before). A chain is complete once its used length reaches chain.length, so a rule costing 2 makes a chain 'shorter' by one extra node every time it is drawn - e.g. a circle with cost 2 leaves room for one stroke fewer. 0 makes the rule free: it never counts towards the length (a chain is still stopped at 64 nodes). The start node always counts 1. Closing a loop does not cost.

arc.description: direction Arc only: which arcs may be drawn. Only used when `direction` is Arc.

outlineNodes.description: direction Circle or Arc: extra nodes along the outline. Only used when `direction` is Circle or Arc.

curve.description: How the edges this rule makes are bent when drawn. Only used when `direction` is Orthogonal, Diagonal, Both, Any or Angle.

ConnectionRuleConfig.description: One weighted connection template a chain can grow with: what direction, how far (in grid units, 1 = adjacent), how likely it is to be picked relative to the stroke's other templates, and how the edges it makes are drawn. A stroke with only one entry still works fine - it's just used 100% of the time since there's nothing to weigh it against.

chance.description: Chance (0-100) that a composite is held to the requirement; rolled once per composite. Default 100.

min.description: How many contacts, counted over the whole composite, are needed. Default 1.

enumDescriptions: A node that two components share (their strokes meet at that point).
An edge of one component cutting through an edge of another. Needs arrangement.crossing.mode NodesOnly, Anywhere or AnywhereButRespectStrict: with None no crossing is ever allowed.
Either of the two (default); only what the crossing mode allows can happen.
markdownEnumDescriptions: A node that two components share (their strokes meet at that point).
An edge of one component cutting through an edge of another. Needs arrangement.crossing.mode NodesOnly, Anywhere or AnywhereButRespectStrict: with None no crossing is ever allowed.
Either of the two (default); only what the crossing mode allows can happen.
kind.description: What counts as a contact. Default Either.

ContactRequirement.description: Asks for components that touch each other (arrangement.contact).

baseGlyphsSheet.description: Also write a sheet of the language's base glyphs, as "_bases/_contact-sheet.png" (the main sheet never contains them). Only has an effect when baseGlyphs is used.

ContactSheetConfig.description: Settings for the contact sheet(s): one PNG laying a language's glyphs out in a grid.

enumDescriptions: Finds the longest run of consecutive edges that continue in one straight line (horizontal, vertical or diagonal) and flips ACROSS it: a horizontal run gives a left-right mirror, a vertical run a top-bottom one, a diagonal run the matching diagonal mirror.
Compares the average of the origin's nodes with the middle of the board and mirrors along the axis where they differ most; the copy is then pushed toward the middle (see 'toward').
markdownEnumDescriptions: Finds the longest run of consecutive edges that continue in one straight line (horizontal, vertical or diagonal) and flips ACROSS it: a horizontal run gives a left-right mirror, a vertical run a top-bottom one, a diagonal run the matching diagonal mirror.
Compares the average of the origin's nodes with the middle of the board and mirrors along the axis where they differ most; the copy is then pushed toward the middle (see 'toward').

enumDescriptions: The mirror line is perpendicular to the run: a horizontal run gives a left-right mirror, so the copy continues the run backwards.
The mirror line is parallel to the run: a horizontal run gives a top-bottom mirror, so the copy lies beside the run (give it a gap, or it lies on top of it).
Either of the two, drawn at random for each copy.
markdownEnumDescriptions: The mirror line is perpendicular to the run: a horizontal run gives a left-right mirror, so the copy continues the run backwards.
The mirror line is parallel to the run: a horizontal run gives a top-bottom mirror, so the copy lies beside the run (give it a gap, or it lies on top of it).
Either of the two, drawn at random for each copy.
axis.description: LongestStraight only: whether the mirror line runs perpendicular to the longest run (default), parallel to it, or either at random. With Parallel the copy lies beside the run, so it needs a gap of 1 or more to clear it. Only used when `by` is LongestStraight.

enumDescriptions: Toward the middle of the board.
Away from the middle, toward the nearest edge.

flips.description: Flip: Random only - the flips to draw from. Default: Horizontal, Vertical, Rotate180. Only used when `flip` is Random.

auto.description: Flip: Auto only - the rule that picks the flip. Only used when `flip` is Auto.

gap.description: Steps the copy is moved away from the origin, along the direction it was flipped toward: 0 puts the copy's start on the anchor itself (the two share that node), 1 or more moves them apart, a negative number pushes the copy back over the origin so the two overlap or cross. Drawn from this range for each copy. Default 0 to 0.

shift.description: Steps the copy is slid sideways (across the gap direction), up or down at random. Drawn from this range, then given a random sign. Default 0 to 0.

enumDescriptions: The start node of the origin chain itself (the copy grows from the same point).
A node that is already on the glyph, picked at random from the ones that work.
A lattice point on a line that is already on the glyph (its ends included), picked at random from the ones that work.

anchor.description: Where the copy's start node goes before gap and shift.

preferNoCrossing.description: Try every flip position the config allows in random order and take one that crosses nothing already drawn. If none exists the best attempt is kept, but only when the destination's arrangement.crossing allows crossing (mode NodesOnly or Anywhere); otherwise the copy fails like any shape that cannot be placed. Turn off to take the first position that obeys the hard rules.

moveGlyphToFit.description: When no position keeps the copy on the grid (but one would, if the strokes already drawn sat somewhere else), the whole glyph so far is moved over, together with the copy, to where it fits. Turn off to fail instead. Not available to copies added by a derivation step, whose glyph keeps its source's position.

regenerateBase.description: First retry: when no position works for the copy, redraw the base shape (the first shape in this chain of copies that is not itself a copy) with fresh random numbers and try again, up to this many times. Everything placed after the base is rebuilt around the new draw. 0 turns it off. Only helps when the base is generated, not a literal.

redrawGlyph.description: Second retry, after the base redraws are spent: redraw the whole glyph from a fresh seed, up to this many times, before giving up with the error. 0 turns it off. Neither retry applies to copies added by a derivation step.

mirrorCurves.description: The copy's curves are the origin's curves, flipped with it, so the two look like mirror images. Turn off to give the copy curves of its own. (Copies added by a derivation step always draw their own curves.)

respectSelfSpacing.description: Apply the original shape's chain.selfSpacing rules between the copy and the original, as if the copy were more nodes of the same stroke: every node of the copy is measured against every node of the chain it copies (a node the two share is exempt, except in AllNodes mode). Existing and Adjacent both mean "every node of the original" here. The copy's own nodes need no check, a flip keeps their distances. Default false.

selfSpacingIgnoresOriginal.description: With respectSelfSpacing: for Existing and AllNodes rules, leave the original chain out and measure the copy against every OTHER node already in the glyph instead (the original's own nodes do not count, so the copy may sit as close to it as arrangement allows). Adjacent rules still compare with the original. Default false. Only used when `respectSelfSpacing` is true.

CopyConfig.description: Turns a shape into a copy of another shape (put it on the destination entry in the shapes list; the origin entry must come earlier in the list). Instead of being drawn, the destination becomes one copy of every instance of the origin, flipped around the origin chain's start node and then moved by the anchor, gap and shift. A copy can itself be copied. The destination takes no chain, nodes, placement or count of its own; its arrangement (crossing, spacing, bias) decides which copy positions are acceptable.

shape.description: Id of the shape whose instances are counted in each component.

enumDescriptions: Strokes of components whose count of the shape differs are not compared at all.
The window radius (and minDistance) is multiplied by factor for such a pair.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Strokes of components whose count of the shape differs are not compared at all.

action.description: Skip: leave the pair out of the rule. Loosen: shrink the rule's window and minDistance by factor.

factor.description: Loosen: multiplier (0-1) for the window radius and minDistance of that pair. Default 0.5. Only used when `action` is Loosen.

CountDiffersConfig.description: Skip or loosen a rule for a pair of strokes whose components rolled a different number of instances of a shape (two bases with 1 and 3 dots are told apart by the count already).

Edges may cross anywhere.

mode.description: Whether this shape's strokes may cross others: None, NodesOnly (only near a node) or Anywhere (see the values).

nodeTolerance.description: NodesOnly: how far (lattice units) from a node a crossing may lie and still count as being at it. A stroke passing near a node but not through it is fine. Default 0.3. Only used when `mode` is NodesOnly.

nodesOfShapes.description: NodesOnly: only the nodes of these shapes (ids) count. Empty/missing = every node (the shape's own included). With a list, the shape's own nodes count only if its own id is listed. Only used when `mode` is NodesOnly.

CrossingConfig.description: Crossing rules of one shape (arrangement.crossing). Curves are taken into account.

edge.description: Curve settings for edges that no connection rule made (the edges of Literal shapes).

proximityGuard.description: A safety net that draws edges straight when a curve could swing into nearby ink. Off by default.

forceAllEdgesCurved.description: Plans EVERY edge as a curve: ignores every chanceToBeCurved and the proximity guard (both would otherwise force edges straight), so "curved" really means curved everywhere. Whether an edge visibly bends still depends on tension: a 0..0 tension band gives a bezier that looks straight. Must not be combined with a chanceToBeCurved below 100 or an enabled guard (the loader rejects that, since they would be silently overridden). Default false.

enumDescriptions: The normal curve plan is used both alone and as a component.
Every edge is a straight line, alone and as a component.
Curve plan when drawn alone, straight lines as a component of a composite.
Straight lines when drawn alone, curve plan as a component of a composite.

contextMode.description: Whether glyphs are curved when drawn alone and when used as a component of a composite. Default AllCurved.

CurveConfig.description: Rendering-time curve behavior that is NOT per edge. How an edge bends (chance, mode, tension, jitter) is set on the connection rule that made it - see the `curve` block of a connection rule. Kept independent of the underlying straight-edge grid topology (which is what intersection checks always operate on): this only affects how the final glyph is drawn, never whether a connection is valid.

enabled.description: Turns the guard on. Default false.

minEdgeLength.description: Edges shorter than this (grid units) are always forced straight - a curve on a very short edge exaggerates its bulge relative to the edge's own length, making it more likely to swing into nearby geometry.

CurveProximityGuardConfig.description: Forces an edge straight based on geometry, independent of the edge's curve settings - a safety net against a curve bulging into nearby ink (a curve on a short edge swings out more). Disabled by default since it changes how many edges end up curved vs. the language's other settings alone would produce.

percent.description: Percentage (0-100) of all nodes (node steps) or all edges (edge steps) that exist when the step runs, rounded to a whole number. Resolved uniformly in the range. Set exactly one of `percent`, `count`.

count.description: A fixed number of nodes/edges, drawn uniformly (inclusive) from the range. Set exactly one of `percent`, `count`.

DerivationAmount.description: How much a step affects: a percentage of what exists, or a fixed number, each as a range. Set exactly one of Percent and Count.

minEdges.description: The step runs only if the glyph has at least this many edges at that point.

maxEdges.description: The step runs only if the glyph has at most this many edges at that point.

minNodes.description: The step runs only if the glyph has at least this many nodes at that point.

maxNodes.description: The step runs only if the glyph has at most this many nodes at that point.

DerivationCondition.description: A gate on a step: it only runs when the glyph, as it is when the step comes up (after the earlier steps), has a number of edges and nodes within these limits. Every limit that is set must hold; none set = no gate. Nodes are the distinct points, including lone ones; a circle or dot is one edge.

enumDescriptions: Always draws its own angle.
Follows the source when the steps that ran were only Scale, Mirror, Rotate or Nudge (default).
Also follows after DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges and Keep: what is left is a part of the source.
Follows whatever the steps did, Add included.

from.description: The glyph (a name from glyphs or baseGlyphs; plain, composite or itself derived) to start from.

maxSimilarityToSource.description: Quality gate against the source only: the derived glyph may resemble it by at most this much (0-1, same measure as quality.maxSimilarity), so it can't be a copy. 1 turns it off. Against every OTHER glyph the normal quality.maxSimilarity applies. Default 0.9.

DerivationConfig.description: A glyph made from another glyph: the source is generated first, then the steps edit a copy of its strokes (a composite source is flattened to plain strokes). The source itself is left as it was. Edges that survive untouched keep the source's exact curves.

op.description: What the step does. Each op accepts only its own options.

onlyIf.description: Only run the step if the glyph has enough / not too many edges and nodes at that point (see the limits of `onlyIf`). Checked before chance. A skipped step changes nothing and uses no random numbers.

chance.description: Chance (0-100) that the step runs at all. Default 100.

amount.description: DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges, Keep, Nudge: how many. For Keep it is how many edges stay. SplitEdges: how many edges are split (left out = every edge that can be). Only used when `op` is DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges, Keep, Nudge or SplitEdges.

enumDescriptions: Any node.
Free tips: nodes with one edge end.
Nodes with exactly two edge ends, i.e. the middle of a stroke.
Nodes where three or more edge ends meet (strokes sharing a node).

Nodes with exactly two edge ends, i.e. the middle of a stroke.

target.description: DeleteNodes, Nudge: which nodes may be picked. Default Any. Only used when `op` is DeleteNodes or Nudge.

enumDescriptions: The node and its edges are removed; a stroke through it splits in two.

For a node in the middle of a stroke, the two neighbours are reconnected with a new path grown from the step's connectionRules (at most bridgeMaxMoves moves, crossing nothing). If no path exists the node is cut instead. Tips and junctions are always cut.

For a node in the middle of a stroke, the two neighbours are reconnected with a new path grown from the step's connectionRules (at most bridgeMaxMoves moves, crossing nothing). If no path exists the node is cut instead. Tips and junctions are always cut.

mode.description: DeleteNodes: Cut (default) or Bridge. Only used when `op` is DeleteNodes.

connectionRules.description: DeleteNodes with Mode Bridge: the moves a replacement path may be built from. Same options as chain.connectionRules (Circle rules are ignored). Only used when `mode` is Bridge.

bridgeMaxMoves.description: DeleteNodes with Mode Bridge: most moves a replacement path may have. Default 3. Only used when `mode` is Bridge.

removeOrphanNodes.description: DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges, Keep: also remove nodes left with no edge. Default true. If false they stay as lone nodes (invisible when drawn, but they still count as nodes for later steps, for similarity, and in the debug view). Only used when `op` is DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges or Keep.

keepAtLeast.description: DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges, Keep: never end with fewer edges than this (picks that would are skipped). Default 1. Only used when `op` is DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges or Keep.

keepConnected.description: DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges, Keep: skip any pick that would split the glyph into more connected pieces than it had before the step. Default false. Only used when `op` is DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges or Keep.

shapes.description: Add: ids of entries of the language's shapes, each placed as it would be in a plain glyph (its count, chain, placement and arrangement), against the strokes that are left. Added strokes may cross the existing ones only if the shape's arrangement.crossing says so. Only used when `op` is Add.

optional.description: Add: if a shape cannot be placed, skip it instead of failing. Default false. Only used when `op` is Add.

factors.description: Scale: weighted ratios, one is picked. A ratio that would not fit the grid is not picked. Only used when `op` is Scale.

enumDescriptions: Left becomes right.
Top becomes bottom.
One of the two, at random.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Left becomes right.
Top becomes bottom.
One of the two, at random.

axis.description: Mirror: default Horizontal. Only used when `op` is Mirror.

degrees.description: Rotate: the allowed rotations (90, 180, 270); one is picked. Default all three. Only used when `op` is Rotate.

distance.description: Nudge: how far a node may move on each axis. Default 1. Only used when `op` is Nudge.

parts.description: SplitEdges: into how many pieces each chosen edge is cut, drawn per edge from the range (2 = one new node). Default 2. Only used when `op` is SplitEdges.

enumDescriptions: As evenly as the lattice allows: the pieces are as close to the same length as possible.
At random places along the edge.
markdownEnumDescriptions: As evenly as the lattice allows: the pieces are as close to the same length as possible.
At random places along the edge.

distribution.description: SplitEdges: Equal (default) or Random places along the edge. Only used when `op` is SplitEdges.

enumDescriptions: Only nodes that lie exactly on the edge are used (the lattice points the edge passes over). The edge keeps its shape; an edge that passes over no free lattice point is left alone. This is the default.
The ideal place is moved to the nearest lattice point, so the edge becomes a slightly bent path through these points (an approximation). See maxDeviation.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Only nodes that lie exactly on the edge are used (the lattice points the edge passes over). The edge keeps its shape; an edge that passes over no free lattice point is left alone. This is the default.

snap.description: SplitEdges: Exact (default, only nodes lying on the edge) or Nearest (approximate, see maxDeviation). Only used when `op` is SplitEdges.

maxDeviation.description: SplitEdges with Snap Nearest: a node whose nearest lattice point is further than this from the original edge is not used. Default 0.75 (about the most a rounded point can be off). Only used when `snap` is Nearest.

minEdgeLength.description: SplitEdges: only edges at least this long (in lattice units) are split. Default 2. Only used when `op` is SplitEdges.

DerivationStep.description: One step of a derivation. A single class for every op, so only the options that belong to the op are allowed (the loader rejects the others).

chanceToBeCurved.description: Chance (0-100) that an edge made by this rule is drawn as a curve; otherwise it is a straight line. Rolled per edge. Default 0 = every edge straight; 100 = always curved (a 0..0 tension still looks straight). This replaces the old language-wide straightLineBias (chanceToBeCurved = 100 - straightLineBias).

enumDescriptions: Tangents inferred from neighboring node angles (smooth-spline feel).
Each node stores its own randomized in/out tangent.
Mix of both, per-node.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Tangents inferred from neighboring node angles (smooth-spline feel).
Each node stores its own randomized in/out tangent.
Mix of both, per-node.
mode.description: How the edge's end tangents are chosen. Derived: from the neighbouring nodes (smooth spline feel). Explicit: each end gets its own randomized tangent. Hybrid: Derived or Explicit per edge, at random.

tension.description: Bezier handle length as a fraction of the edge length; each handle draws its own value. Only used when `chanceToBeCurved` is above 0 (with 0 no edge is ever curved).

explicitJitterDegrees.description: Explicit/Hybrid: max angle (degrees) an end tangent may deviate from the derived one. Only used when `mode` is Explicit or Hybrid.

EdgeCurveConfig.description: How ONE edge is bent when drawn. Each connection rule carries its own copy, so a rule can make long edges gentle curves and short ticks dead straight within the same stroke. Edges that come from no rule (Literal shapes) use curve.edge instead. Only affects drawing - never whether a connection is valid.

max.description: Highest value (inclusive). Must not be below min.

FloatRange.description: A plain floating-point range (no percent semantics), resolved the same way as the integer and percent ranges. Used for render settings expressed as canvas fractions, degrees, tension, etc.

glyph.description: The glyph (from glyphs or baseGlyphs) whose nodes are used. It is drawn before the glyph this shape is drawn in, and drawn again (with this glyph after it) whenever it is redrawn. "*" = every other glyph that is not a composite and comes earlier in baseGlyphs / glyphs.

offset.description: Added to every node of that glyph, as [x, y]: where the glyph sits relative to this one. Default [0, 0].

GlyphNodes.description: The nodes of another glyph, moved by an offset (shape masks only).

width.description: Number of lattice columns (nodes along x). Default 25.

height.description: Number of lattice rows (nodes along y). Default 25.

GridConfig.description: The lattice a language is drawn on: nodes lie at whole coordinates from 0 to width-1 and height-1.

max.description: Highest value (inclusive). Must not be below min.

IntRange.description: An inclusive integer range, resolved to one concrete value per generation via the deterministic per-glyph random source (so re-running the same config+seed always resolves to the same value).

angle.description: Degrees, 0 to 180, inclusive at both ends.

outer.description: Replacement outer join, or omitted to keep the context's.

inner.description: Replacement inner join, or omitted to keep the context's.

JoinAngleRule.description: Replaces the outer and/or inner join for nodes whose angle falls in a range.

outer.description: The convex outside of the bend.

inner.description: The notch between two strokes. Overlap (the default) leaves it as it is.

byAngle.description: Overrides for particular angles, tried in order; the first rule whose angle range contains the angle wins, and whatever it leaves out falls back to outer / inner above. The angle is the one between the two strokes: 180 = straight on, 90 = a right angle, 45 = a sharp turn. On the grid that is almost always 45, 90 or 135; on curves it varies.

JoinContextConfig.description: The outer and inner join for one kind of node, plus optional per-angle overrides.

enumDescriptions: Outer: a sharp point. Inner: leaves the notch as it is.
A flat cut across the corner (outer) or chamfer across the notch (inner).
An arc (outer) or fillet (inner).
Nothing added: plain overlapping strokes.
Outer only: the miter point cut flat along levelAxis.

style.description: How the join is drawn (Miter, Bevel, Round, Overlap, Level). Outer and inner sides read the styles differently; see the values.

miterLimit.description: Outer Miter only: beyond this point-length / half-width ratio a miter falls back to a bevel. Only used when `style` is Miter.

size.description: Inner Bevel / Round only: chamfer length or fillet radius, in half-widths of the stroke (1 = as large as half the stroke width). Limited automatically so it never reaches past the neighbouring node. Only used when `style` is Bevel or Round.

enumDescriptions: Across the stroke's dominant direction (a cap) or the join's outward direction (a join).
Cut along the row.
Cut along the column.
Cut along row and column, so a diagonal end becomes a point with one horizontal and one vertical face.

Cut along the row.
