Cut along row and column, so a diagonal end becomes a point with one horizontal and one vertical face.
axis.description: Outer Level only: the line the corner is cut along. Auto = across the corner's outward direction, so a V pointing down is cut flat on the bottom and a corner pointing right is cut along its column. Only used when `style` is Level.

JoinSideConfig.description: One side (outer or inner) of a join.

JoinsConfig.description: How strokes are joined, for every typeface. A "corner" is a bend within one stroke; a "junction" is any node where strokes meet (tip to tip, a tip on another stroke, a crossing, a stroke revisiting its own node). Each has an OUTER side (the convex outside of the bend, where ink is added to make a point or round) and an INNER side (the notch between two strokes, which can be filled with a chamfer or fillet).

trimCaps.description: If true, tips that end at a junction (a node where another stroke is also present) are drawn without their caps, Ball terminals or start blobs, and the joins above fill the node instead. A tip that stands alone keeps all of them. With outer Overlap nothing fills the node, so pair this with Miter, Bevel or Round.

straightenInnerDegrees.description: 0 = off. Where two strokes meet within this many degrees of straight (180) and the NOTCH between them (the side that bends inwards, under 180 degrees) has no other stroke in it, that notch is filled with a long chamfer (see straightenLength) so the edge reads as one straight line instead of a kink. Other strokes may leave the node on the other side. Replaces the inner join for those notches.

straightenOuterDegrees.description: 0 = off. The same for the OUTSIDE of the bend (the side that bends outwards, over 180 degrees), e.g. the top of a T whose bar is slightly bent that way. Ink cannot be removed, so instead the edges are extended along one straight line through the corner and the thin wedges between that line and the real edges are filled; each wedge ends in a small step whose height grows with the angle and with straightenLength. Replaces the outer join for those gaps.

straightenLength.description: Length of the straightening fill along each stroke's edge, in half-widths. Limited automatically so it never reaches past the neighbouring node.

outer.description: The convex outside of the bend.

inner.description: The notch between two strokes. Overlap (the default) leaves it as it is.

byAngle.description: Overrides for particular angles, tried in order; the first rule whose angle range contains the angle wins, and whatever it leaves out falls back to outer / inner above. The angle is the one between the two strokes: 180 = straight on, 90 = a right angle, 45 = a sharp turn. On the grid that is almost always 45, 90 or 135; on curves it varies.

JunctionJoinConfig.description: The join settings for strokes meeting at a node: everything a corner has, plus how the tips that end there are treated.

name.description: The language's name. Its random seed is derived from it, so renaming a language changes every glyph.

canvas.description: Size of each rendered glyph image and its margin.

grid.description: The lattice this language's glyphs are drawn on. Required per language.

items.description: A glyph name, e.g. "warrior" (the older { "name": "warrior" } form also loads).

glyphs.description: The language's real glyphs - these end up in the output atlas/contact sheet.

items.description: A glyph name, e.g. "warrior" (the older { "name": "warrior" } form also loads).

baseGlyphs.description: Glyphs that exist only to be components of combination recipes. Generated (before Glyphs, so recipes can use them) and rendered, but written to a separate "_bases" folder and left out of the contact sheet. They go through the same quality/similarity gate as every other glyph.

usageSizeBias.description: Glyphs used in more recipes roll lower counts/lengths, for shapes that have a count (guaranteed shapes are unaffected).

shapes.description: What every plain (non-composite) glyph is built from, placed in list order: each entry carries its own chain rules, placement and arrangement. A guaranteed motif is an entry without a count; free-form strokes are entries with one.

curve.description: Curve settings that are not per edge: edges no rule made, the proximity guard, and curves in composites.

combination.description: How composite glyphs are built from components: recipes, scale and rotation, and the arrangement rules.

derivations.description: Glyphs made by editing another glyph, by glyph name. A name listed here is not generated from shapes and has no recipe. Each entry has a `from` glyph and a list of `steps`.

quality.description: Post-generation gates (similarity to other glyphs, straight-line rejection).

render.description: Rendering (framing, colours, typeface). Pixel size/margin come from Canvas.

LanguageDefinition.description: One language: its glyph lists, shapes, recipes, derivations, quality checks and rendering.

allow.description: Regions a node may be in. A node is usable when it is in at least one of them (no list = everywhere).

forbid.description: Regions a node may not be in. A node in any of them is not usable.

NodeMaskConfig.description: placement.nodes: which lattice nodes a shape may use (every node of its strokes, and where it starts). A node is usable when it is in at least one allow region (or allow is empty) and in no forbid region, and inside placement.bounds and the grid.

x.description: Which x coordinates match. Left out = all.

y.description: Which y coordinates match. Left out = all.

NodePattern.description: Nodes picked by their coordinates: a node matches when its x matches x AND its y matches y (an axis left out matches everything).

points.description: These nodes, as [x, y] pairs. Set exactly one of `points`, `box`, `pattern`, `nodesOfShapes`, `boundsOfShapes`, `nodesOfComponents`, `nodesOfGlyph`.

box.description: Every node inside this inclusive box. Set exactly one of `points`, `box`, `pattern`, `nodesOfShapes`, `boundsOfShapes`, `nodesOfComponents`, `nodesOfGlyph`.

pattern.description: Nodes picked by pattern (odd / even / every n-th x and y). Set exactly one of `points`, `box`, `pattern`, `nodesOfShapes`, `boundsOfShapes`, `nodesOfComponents`, `nodesOfGlyph`.

nodesOfShapes.description: The nodes of these shapes (the node pool): only nodes that already exist in the glyph. Set exactly one of `points`, `box`, `pattern`, `nodesOfShapes`, `boundsOfShapes`, `nodesOfComponents`, `nodesOfGlyph`.

boundsOfShapes.description: Everything inside the box around the nodes of these shapes. Set exactly one of `points`, `box`, `pattern`, `nodesOfShapes`, `boundsOfShapes`, `nodesOfComponents`, `nodesOfGlyph`.

nodesOfComponents.description: Combination placements only: the nodes of components placed earlier, optionally only those of some shapes inside them. Set exactly one of `points`, `box`, `pattern`, `nodesOfShapes`, `boundsOfShapes`, `nodesOfComponents`, `nodesOfGlyph`.

nodesOfGlyph.description: Shape masks only: the nodes of another glyph (see glyph), moved by offset - for a shape that should start or end where another glyph has a node. The other glyph is drawn first. Set exactly one of `points`, `box`, `pattern`, `nodesOfShapes`, `boundsOfShapes`, `nodesOfComponents`, `nodesOfGlyph`.

NodeRegion.description: One set of nodes. Exactly one of the fields is set.

enumDescriptions: No extra nodes (the default).
A node at each angle of the preset that the circle or arc covers.
A node on every lattice point the outline passes within the tolerance of.
markdownEnumDescriptions: No extra nodes (the default).
A node at each angle of the preset that the circle or arc covers.
A node on every lattice point the outline passes within the tolerance of.
mode.description: Which extra lattice points on a circle or arc count as its nodes: None, AtAngles or EveryLatticePoint.

enumDescriptions: All eight of the above.
markdownEnumDescriptions: All eight of the above.
angles.description: AtAngles: which angles get a node. Default Cardinal. Only used when `mode` is AtAngles.

enumDescriptions: Put the node on the nearest lattice point if it is within the tolerance; otherwise skip that angle.
Always put the node on the nearest lattice point, however far it is.
Only where the point is exactly on a lattice point.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Put the node on the nearest lattice point if it is within the tolerance; otherwise skip that angle.
Always put the node on the nearest lattice point, however far it is.
Only where the point is exactly on a lattice point.
snap.description: AtAngles: how a point between lattice points is handled. Default Within. Only used when `mode` is AtAngles.

tolerance.description: How close (lattice units) the outline must pass to a lattice point for Within and EveryLatticePoint. Default 0.3. Only used when `mode` is AtAngles or EveryLatticePoint.

OutlineNodesConfig.description: Extra nodes along a circle or arc (on a connection rule with direction Circle or Arc). They count as nodes of the shape for spacing, startOnExistingNode and NodesOnly crossings; the chain itself still continues from the far node.

max.description: Highest percentage (0-100). Must not be below min.

PercentRange.description: A percentage hint (0-100), resolved the same way as an integer range. Used as a soft bias (e.g. a chance), not a hard constraint.

minX.description: Smallest x a node may have (inclusive).

minY.description: Smallest y a node may have (inclusive).

maxX.description: Largest x a node may have (inclusive).

maxY.description: Largest y a node may have (inclusive).

PlacementBounds.description: An inclusive box of lattice node coordinates (placement.bounds).

enumDescriptions: Exact origin every time (`fixedOrigin` is required, and must lie on the grid - the config loader checks both). With nothing else varying (a Literal motif, no rotation) the resolver makes a single attempt whatever `maxPlacementAttempts` says, since retrying would just re-check an identical result.
Random anchor point, retried up to `maxPlacementAttempts` on collision.
Anchored exactly at (Width / 2, Height / 2) of the grid (integer division, so the upper-middle cell on even sizes); still collision-checked.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Exact origin every time (`fixedOrigin` is required, and must lie on the grid - the config loader checks both). With nothing else varying (a Literal motif, no rotation) the resolver makes a single attempt whatever `maxPlacementAttempts` says, since retrying would just re-check an identical result.
Random anchor point, retried up to `maxPlacementAttempts` on collision.
Anchored exactly at (Width / 2, Height / 2) of the grid (integer division, so the upper-middle cell on even sizes); still collision-checked.
mode.description: Where the shape starts: RandomValid (default), Fixed (an exact origin) or CenterAnchor (the middle of the grid).

oneOf.description: One origin, or an array of origins from which one is picked at random.

fixedOrigin.description: Required when Mode == Fixed, and an error with any other mode (it would be ignored). Written as { "x": 7, "y": 9 } or [7, 9] - or as an array of such points, in which case one is picked at random for each glyph (a failed try moves on to the next of a shuffled order, so every origin is tried before giving up). Required when `mode` is Fixed. Only used when `mode` is Fixed.

discardUsedOrigins.description: Fixed with several fixedOrigin points: an origin an earlier instance of this shape (same glyph) was placed at is not used again, so a shape with count N and N origins fills each of them once. When every origin is used the instance cannot be placed. Default false. Only used when `mode` is Fixed.

bounds.description: A box smaller than the grid that this shape must stay inside, treated as the edge of the grid while the shape is generated and placed (nodes, and circles' whole outlines). Inclusive node coordinates, e.g. { "minX": 4, "minY": 4, "maxX": 10, "maxY": 10 }. Other shapes are not limited by it. null = the whole grid.

nodes.description: Which nodes this shape may use, beyond Bounds: direct nodes, boxes, odd/even/every-n patterns, the nodes of other shapes, or the box around other shapes. Every node of the shape's strokes (circle nodes included) must pass, and so must the node it starts on. Not applied to copyOf shapes. null = no restriction.

allowRotationOnPlace.description: Allows a random rotation per attempt, from Rotations (below). Only Literal motifs are affected: a generated chain is already random and ignores the rotation.

rotations.description: The angles (0/90/180/270) this placement may rotate by - meaningful only for a Literal motif's placement; the loader rejects it anywhere else. null (default) = inherit Combination.Rotation when Combination.`allowRotate` is on, which is the original coupling; a list = use exactly these; an empty list = never rotate.

maxPlacementAttempts.description: Failure budget for "find/fit a shape at a location" — distinct from `combination.maxRetriesPerRecipe`, which governs "can this recipe's components work together at all". Keeping these separate lets failure messages say precisely which stage gave up.

redoShape.description: When an instance of this shape cannot be placed within maxPlacementAttempts: how many times to redraw ALL instances of this shape (new chains, new positions) before giving up on this try of the glyph. Earlier shapes stay as they are. Default 0 = no redraw (the glyph fails, as before).

redrawGlyph.description: After redoShape is spent: how many times to redraw the WHOLE glyph from a fresh seed (every shape again) before the failure is reported. Default 0.

startOnExistingNode.description: RandomValid only: start the shape on a node already in the glyph (chosen uniformly) instead of a random grid point, so shapes grow out of each other. Needs no crossing permission - edges that merely meet at a node don't count as crossing - but can't be combined with `arrangement.spacing.minNodeDistance` above 0 (a shared node is distance 0). Only used when `mode` is RandomValid.

startOnExistingNodeChance.description: With startOnExistingNode: the chance (0-100) that an attempt starts on an existing node; otherwise it starts on a random grid point as usual. Rolled per attempt. Default 100 = always start on a node. Only used when `startOnExistingNode` is true.

startOnShapes.description: With startOnExistingNode: only the nodes of these shapes (ids of EARLIER shapes) count as places to start on. null (default) = every node already in the glyph. When none of the listed shapes was drawn in this glyph, there is nothing to attach to and the shape is placed like the first one, at a random point. Only used when `startOnExistingNode` is true.

side.description: RandomValid only: pull the shape towards a side or corner of the glyph. null = no pull. It ranks the shape's best-of-N candidates (arrangement.candidates), so raise that for a stronger pull. Only used when `mode` is RandomValid.

PlacementConfig.description: Where a shape goes: its start point (mode), how often placing it is retried, an optional box it must stay in, and whether it grows out of nodes that are already in the glyph.

maxSimilarity.description: Jaccard similarity (0-1) of two glyphs' normalized shapes, at or above which they're considered too similar and one gets regenerated. 1.0 (or higher) disables the check entirely. Default 0.7 matches "no more than 70% alike".

rejectStraightLineOnly.description: Reject a glyph whose entire geometry (across all its chains/components) reduces to a single straight line with no bends.

enumDescriptions: Which nodes they use. Two glyphs that touch the same nodes are alike however the nodes are joined (the original behaviour).
Which strokes they draw: the lines, circles and arcs between nodes. Glyphs on the same few nodes still differ when they join them differently.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Which nodes they use. Two glyphs that touch the same nodes are alike however the nodes are joined (the original behaviour).
Which strokes they draw: the lines, circles and arcs between nodes. Glyphs on the same few nodes still differ when they join them differently.
similarityBasis.description: What `maxSimilarity` compares: the nodes (default) or the strokes. Edges is the one to use when glyphs are built on a small fixed set of nodes (a node mask), where nearly every glyph uses the same nodes. Only used when `maxSimilarity` is below 1 (1 turns the similarity check off).

comparePosition.description: false (default): two glyphs are compared after shifting each so its bounding box starts at the origin, so the same shape in another place counts as alike. true: compared where they lie on the grid (for glyphs whose position means something, like coordinates).

maxRegenerationAttempts.description: How many times a glyph that fails a quality check is redrawn before the run fails (or, for Score rules, keeps the best attempt). Default 10.

compositeMaxSimilarity.description: Similarity limit for COMPOSITES, checked only against other composites - never against plain or base glyphs, which a composite contains by construction. 1.0 or more (the default) = composites are not compared at all, as before. A composite at or above the limit is rebuilt with a fresh seed, up to `maxRegenerationAttempts`. Composites are never subject to `rejectStraightLineOnly`.

rules.description: Declarative checks of every finished glyph (see the fields of a rule). Evaluated after the similarity and straight-line checks, in order. Default: none.

pairRules.description: Checks BETWEEN glyphs (same fields as `rules`; the selectors name glyphs): the strokes of one glyph are judged against the strokes of another, e.g. the dots of two base glyphs that never share a composite. Checked when a glyph is accepted, against every glyph already built. Default: none.

acceptPenalty.description: Score rules: the penalty at or below which a glyph is accepted at once. A glyph above it is retried (up to `maxRegenerationAttempts`) and the lowest-penalty attempt is kept if none gets under it. Default 0. Only used when a rule or pair rule has `onFail` Score.

QualityConfig.description: Checks a finished glyph must pass (similarity, straight lines, declarative rules) and how often it is redrawn when it fails.

id.description: A name for the rule, shown in warnings and errors. Must be unique.

enumDescriptions: Plain and composite glyphs.
Plain (non-composite) glyphs only.
Composite glyphs only.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Plain and composite glyphs.
Plain (non-composite) glyphs only.
Composite glyphs only.
appliesTo.description: Which glyphs the rule checks: Both (default), Plain or Composite.

onlyForGlyphs.description: Only these glyphs (by name). Empty/missing = every glyph.

subject.description: The strokes that are checked: filtered by shape, form and (in pairRules) glyph.

against.description: The strokes the subject is compared with. Same filters as subject.

enumDescriptions: Composite glyphs: strokes of the other components. Plain glyphs: strokes of other chains.
Composites only: strokes that belong to another component. A plain glyph is not checked by the rule.
Any stroke that is not part of the subject's own chain.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Composite glyphs: strokes of the other components. Plain glyphs: strokes of other chains.
Composites only: strokes that belong to another component. A plain glyph is not checked by the rule.
Any stroke that is not part of the subject's own chain.
among.description: Which strokes count as 'something else' for the subject (see the values). Default Auto.

enumDescriptions: How many of the 'against' strokes lie in the window (at most max, default 0).
How many of the 'against' strokes in the window LOOK LIKE the subject (similarity at or above similarityThreshold); at most max, default 0.
The nearest 'against' stroke is at least minDistance away.
markdownEnumDescriptions: How many of the 'against' strokes lie in the window (at most max, default 0).
How many of the 'against' strokes in the window LOOK LIKE the subject (similarity at or above similarityThreshold); at most max, default 0.
The nearest 'against' stroke is at least minDistance away.
measure.description: What is judged: Count of strokes in the window, Similar strokes in the window, or the Distance to the nearest stroke.

window.description: Count and Similar: the area around the subject that is searched. Only used when `measure` is Count or Similar.

max.description: Count and Similar: how many strokes may be found before the check fails. Default 0. Only used when `measure` is Count or Similar.

minDistance.description: Distance: the nearest 'against' stroke must be at least this far (lattice units). Only used when `measure` is Distance.

enumDescriptions: What the strokes look like: both are drawn with a brush of strokeWidth cells, centred on each other, and the overlap (intersection over union) is the similarity.
Same kind of stroke and about the same size (lines and curves: length within 1 cell; arcs: sweep within 45 degrees and diameter within 1 cell). 1 or 0.
markdownEnumDescriptions: What the strokes look like: both are drawn with a brush of strokeWidth cells, centred on each other, and the overlap (intersection over union) is the similarity.
Same kind of stroke and about the same size (lines and curves: length within 1 cell; arcs: sweep within 45 degrees and diameter within 1 cell). 1 or 0.
similarity.description: Similar: how the strokes are compared. Default Visual. Only used when `measure` is Similar.

similarityThreshold.description: Similar: similarity (0-1) at or above which two strokes count as alike. Default 0.7. Only used when `measure` is Similar.

strokeWidth.description: Visual similarity: brush width in lattice units. Default 1.5. Only used when `measure` is Similar.

enumDescriptions: The glyph is rejected and regenerated (fresh seed), like a too-similar glyph.
The glyph is kept; the problem is reported as a warning at the end of the run.

A soft score: every broken check adds weight to the glyph's penalty. A glyph with a penalty above quality.acceptPenalty is retried, but if no attempt gets under it the best one is kept instead of failing.
markdownEnumDescriptions: The glyph is rejected and regenerated (fresh seed), like a too-similar glyph.
The glyph is kept; the problem is reported as a warning at the end of the run.

A soft score: every broken check adds weight to the glyph's penalty. A glyph with a penalty above quality.acceptPenalty is retried, but if no attempt gets under it the best one is kept instead of failing.
onFail.description: What a failure does: Reject (redraw), Warn (keep and report) or Score (add weight to the glyph's penalty).

enumDescriptions: Only rearrange the composite (what a quality retry always does).
Also redraw the component that holds the stroke that was judged (the subject).
Also redraw the component that holds the stroke it clashed with.
Redraw the subject's or the other component, alternating from one attempt to the next.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Only rearrange the composite (what a quality retry always does).
Also redraw the component that holds the stroke that was judged (the subject).
Also redraw the component that holds the stroke it clashed with.
Redraw the subject's or the other component, alternating from one attempt to the next.
redo.description: Composites, onFail Reject: what is redrawn when the rule fails. Default Composite. Only used when `onFail` is Reject.

weight.description: Score: the penalty one broken check adds. Default 1. Only used when `onFail` is Score.

whenCountsDiffer.description: Composites: skip or loosen the rule for components that rolled a different count of a shape.

QualityRule.description: One declarative check of a finished glyph (quality.rules): for every stroke picked by subject, look at what lies around it among the strokes picked by against, and judge it with measure.

enumDescriptions: The subject's bounding box grown by radius on every side (a square around a dot).
Everything within radius of the subject's path.
markdownEnumDescriptions: The subject's bounding box grown by radius on every side (a square around a dot).
Everything within radius of the subject's path.
shape.description: The shape of the searched area around the subject: Square or Circle.

QualityWindow.description: The area around a stroke that a rule looks at.

width.description: Stroke width as a fraction of the canvas size; a value is drawn per glyph from the range. Default 0.05.

enumDescriptions: Flat end, square to the stroke.
Flat end extended half a stroke width.
Semicircular end.
Flat end cut along levelAxis (see capLevel).
markdownEnumDescriptions: Flat end, square to the stroke.
Flat end extended half a stroke width.
Semicircular end.
Flat end cut along levelAxis (see capLevel).
cap.description: How a free stroke end is finished: Butt, Square, Round or Level. Default Butt.

enumDescriptions: Across the stroke's dominant direction (a cap) or the join's outward direction (a join).
Cut along the row.
Cut along the column.
Cut along row and column, so a diagonal end becomes a point with one horizontal and one vertical face.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Across the stroke's dominant direction (a cap) or the join's outward direction (a join).
Cut along the row.
Cut along the column.
Cut along row and column, so a diagonal end becomes a point with one horizontal and one vertical face.
capLevel.description: With cap Level: which line the end is cut along. Horizontal = flat on the node's row (like text on a baseline), Vertical = along its column, Auto = across the stroke's dominant direction, so a stroke steeper than 45 degrees is cut horizontally and a flatter one vertically. Straight horizontal and vertical strokes are never changed. Only used when `cap` is Level.

enumDescriptions: Leave the level of the end as it is.
Every Level end grows until its face lies half a stroke width past its node's row (or column).
markdownEnumDescriptions: Leave the level of the end as it is.
Every Level end grows until its face lies half a stroke width past its node's row (or column).
capLevelFlat.description: With cap Level: what happens to an end that is already flat on the axis. ExtendToNeighbours grows every end to half a stroke width past its node's row (or column), so verticals, horizontals and diagonals all stop on one line. Only used when `cap` is Level.

RectangularTypefaceConfig.description: Constant-width strokes. Independent of curve.mode: on a curved edge you simply get a constant-width band following the curve. All widths in this file's configs are fractions of the canvas size, so stroke weight looks the same at any pixel size and in any framing mode.

enumDescriptions: The whole grid maps to the canvas; a glyph's size/position on the grid carries through.
Crop to the glyph's own bounding box and centre it (relative sizes are lost).
Crop to the combined bounding box of every glyph in the language (same scale for all).
Grid's scale, but each glyph re-centred on the canvas.
markdownEnumDescriptions: The whole grid maps to the canvas; a glyph's size/position on the grid carries through.
Crop to the glyph's own bounding box and centre it (relative sizes are lost).
Crop to the combined bounding box of every glyph in the language (same scale for all).
Grid's scale, but each glyph re-centred on the canvas.
framing.description: How a glyph is framed in its image: the whole Grid (default), the Glyph's own box, the whole Language, or GlyphCentered.

rotateDegrees.description: Turns every glyph by this many degrees, clockwise, around the middle of its grid; the canvas itself stays as it is. Any angle works (curves turn exactly). The framing then fits the turned glyphs, so with Grid framing the grid's square is what is rotated and its corners may reach past the canvas margin. Applies to the normal and the debug images alike. Default 0.

rotateOptions.description: Per-glyph random turn, added to rotateDegrees: each glyph draws one option by weight, then an angle uniformly from that option's range (degrees, clockwise). The draw comes from the glyph's own seed, so a glyph always turns the same way. Empty (default) = no random turn. Example: [ { "min": -8, "max": 8, "weight": 4 }, { "min": 85, "max": 95, "weight": 1 } ] mostly tilts a little and now and then lays a glyph on its side.

background.description: #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB; the default is fully transparent.

typeface.description: The stroke style: kind (Rectangular, ThickEnds or Brush) and that kind's own block.

joins.description: How strokes are joined where they bend and where they meet, for every typeface.

contactSheet.description: The overview sheet(s) the CLI writes next to the glyph images.

debugShowNodes.description: Debug option. When any of the debug options is on, the CLI writes an extra "<glyph>.debug.png" next to each normal image, drawn with the enabled overlays (the normal images stay clean; with all of them off no debug files are written). Overlay for checking generation output: the whole lattice as faint dots with coordinates labelled every 5 cells, plus a dot on every node of the glyph - red for a free-form sub-symbol, blue for a guaranteed motif, gold where a node is used more than once (a revisit, or a node shared by shapes).

debugColorComponents.description: Debug option (see `debugShowNodes`): colour each combination component differently in the extra ".debug.png" images.

debugColorParts.description: Debug option (see `debugShowNodes`): in the extra ".debug.png" images, colour the ink each kind of part ADDS on top of the stroke bodies - grey for caps (and Ball / Ink terminals), violet for corner joins, pink for junction joins (including straightening). The strokes themselves keep the foreground colour (or their component colour). Parts are painted over the strokes in the order they are built: corner joins, then junction joins, then caps.

debugColorShapes.description: Debug option (see `debugShowNodes`): in the extra ".debug.png" images, give every shape its own colour, in the order of the shapes list. Instances of one shape (a shape with a count, or a copy of each instance) share its hue and differ in lightness, so they can be told apart. Joins between strokes keep the foreground colour. Takes the place of debugColorComponents where both are on.

debugShowUndrawn.description: Debug option (see `debugShowNodes`): in the extra ".debug.png" images, also draw the shapes that have isDrawn = false, in one translucent orange. They are never in the normal images.

RenderConfig.description: Per-language rendering settings. Pixel size and margin still come from the language's `canvas`.

min.description: Smallest angle in degrees (clockwise; negative turns the other way).

weight.description: Relative chance of this option (default 1; 0 = never).

RotateOption.description: One weighted range of turns for render.rotateOptions.

allowed.description: Angles (0, 90, 180, 270) a component may be rotated by when combination.allowRotate is on. Default [0].

weight.description: One weight shared by every non-zero angle (there are no per-angle weights): how likely a rotated placement is, relative to an unrotated one (weight 1), when the combination search falls back to trying scale/rotation combinations. 1 = rotated as likely as not, 0.5 = half as likely, 0 = never rotate. Multiplies with the scale factor's weight.

RotationConfig.description: Allowed rotation angles for overlay composition. Only 0, 90, 180 and 270 are supported (they keep every node on the grid; any other angle, 45 included, would leave the grid) - the config loader rejects other angles.

numerator.description: Top of the ratio (2 and 3 give 2/3). Must be positive. Default 1.

denominator.description: Bottom of the ratio. Must be positive. A ratio above 1 enlarges, below 1 shrinks (only when every node divides exactly). Default 1.

weight.description: How early this ratio is tried relative to the others. 0 = never used. Default 1.

ScaleFactorConfig.description: One allowed scale factor for overlay composition, expressed as an exact fraction rather than a float — necessary because lattice-safety of shrinking depends on exact divisibility of every node's offset from the component's anchor, which a float range can't express or validate cleanly. The check is made per component: a shrinking factor is only usable if every node's coordinates divide exactly for the specific shape being scaled, so "nicer" geometry (lots of even-length edges) naturally shrinks more often than oddly shaped components, without the generator having to force it. Weight orders the fallback search: heavier factors are tried earlier (it multiplies with Rotation.Weight for a rotated placement); 0 = never use this factor. With every weight equal the order is a plain uniform shuffle.

enumDescriptions: MIN: at least the distance from every earlier node EXCEPT the one it connects from (that gap is set by the connection rules) and except an exact revisit of an existing node. MAX: within the distance of every earlier node, connecting-from node included.

Only the last Lookback nodes of the chain (1 = just the node it connects from, 2 = also the one before that, ...). Constrains the local shape of the stroke - e.g. a minimum here forces steps/turns to be at least that long. An exact revisit of one of those nodes is exempt from the minimum.

EVERY earlier node, no exemptions at all. For a MIN this also means the connecting step must be at least that long and an exact node revisit is impossible (distance 0). For a MAX it behaves the same as Existing.
markdownEnumDescriptions: MIN: at least the distance from every earlier node EXCEPT the one it connects from (that gap is set by the connection rules) and except an exact revisit of an existing node. MAX: within the distance of every earlier node, connecting-from node included.

Only the last Lookback nodes of the chain (1 = just the node it connects from, 2 = also the one before that, ...). Constrains the local shape of the stroke - e.g. a minimum here forces steps/turns to be at least that long. An exact revisit of one of those nodes is exempt from the minimum.

EVERY earlier node, no exemptions at all. For a MIN this also means the connecting step must be at least that long and an exact node revisit is impossible (distance 0). For a MAX it behaves the same as Existing.
mode.description: Which earlier nodes a new node is measured against: Existing, Adjacent (the last few) or AllNodes.

minDistance.description: A new node must be at least this far (lattice units) from the nodes the mode checks. 0 = off.

maxDistance.description: A new node must be within this distance (lattice units) of the nodes the mode checks. 0 = off. Must not be below minDistance.

lookback.description: Adjacent mode only: how many of the chain's most recent nodes are checked. Only used when `mode` is Adjacent.

SelfSpacingRule.description: One node-to-node spacing rule applied while a single chain grows. Several rules (even of the same Mode) can be active at once; a new node must satisfy all of them. Distances are in grid units, 0 = that bound is off.

id.description: Unique within the language. Names the shape in error messages and seeds its random streams, so renaming it changes the glyphs.

enumDescriptions: Fixed relative-coordinate shape (nodes), identical every time except for rotation.
Grown by the chain engine from its own chain rules.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Fixed relative-coordinate shape (nodes), identical every time except for rotation.
Grown by the chain engine from its own chain rules.
kind.description: Leave out on a shape with `copyOf` (a copy follows its original).

count.description: How many instances per glyph, rolled once per glyph. Omit for exactly one guaranteed instance (no roll). Leave out on a shape with `copyOf` (a copy follows its original).

chance.description: Chance (0-100) that this entry is drawn in a glyph at all, rolled once per glyph and covering every instance (a count still applies when it is drawn). Default 100: always drawn. A copy shape whose original was skipped has nothing to copy and is skipped too.

onlyForGlyphs.description: When set, this shape is drawn only in these glyphs (names from glyphs/baseGlyphs); null = every plain glyph. A copy of this shape is drawn only where this shape is.

excludeGlyphs.description: Glyphs this shape is never drawn in (applied after `onlyForGlyphs`). Empty = none.

isDrawn.description: false: the shape is generated and placed like any other - it blocks other shapes, counts for crossing and spacing, and can be copied, derived and combined - but it is left out of the rendered glyph (and out of its framing). Use it as an invisible blockade or spacer. Shown only in the extra debug images, in their own colour, when render.debugShowUndrawn is on. Default true.

chain.description: Chain rules - Generative shapes only. Only used when `kind` is Generative. Leave out on a shape with `copyOf` (a copy follows its original). Leave out on a shape with `chainFrom` (a copy follows its original).

nodes.description: [x, y] points relative to the placement origin - Literal shapes only. Only used when `kind` is Literal. Required when `kind` is Literal. Leave out on a shape with `copyOf` (a copy follows its original).

placement.description: Where the shape goes and how it is rotated. Leave out on a shape with `copyOf` (a copy follows its original).

arrangement.description: How the shape relates to the shapes already placed. On a shape, `crossing.mode` cannot be AnywhereButRespectStrict and `bias.includeScaleAndRotation` must be false (both are for combinations).

seedLabel.description: Advanced: prefix of this shape's random streams, which defaults to "shape-" plus the id. Only needed to make a migrated config reproduce its old glyphs exactly (the migration tool sets it); leave it out otherwise.

chainFrom.description: Id of another generative shape whose whole `chain` block (length, connectionRules, weighting, selfSpacing, loops, revisits) this shape uses instead of one of its own - the shape keeps its own count, placement, arrangement, glyph filters and chance, and draws from its own random stream, so it comes out different. The source may itself use chainFrom (no loops). The source can be anywhere in the list. Leave out `chain` on a shape that uses this; it would be ignored. Generative shapes only. Only used when `kind` is Generative. Leave out on a shape with `copyOf` (a copy follows its original).

copyOf.description: Makes this entry a copy of an earlier shape instead of drawing it (see the `copyOf` block). Leave out kind, count, chain, nodes and placement on such an entry.

ShapeDefinition.description: One entry in a language's shapes list: a kind of stroke every plain glyph is built from. The list is processed in order, each entry placed against everything before it. Omit count for a guaranteed shape (exactly one, always present); give a count range for free-form strokes (rolled per glyph, and the only kind affected by usageSizeBias).

shapes.description: Ids of the shapes (already placed in the glyph when this shape is placed).

margin.description: Lattice units added on every side. Default 0.

ShapesBox.description: The box around the nodes of other shapes, grown by margin on every side.

enumDescriptions: The listed sides.
Sides drawn at random (see Pick) for each instance of the shape, then used like Prefer.
markdownEnumDescriptions: The listed sides.
Sides drawn at random (see Pick) for each instance of the shape, then used like Prefer.
mode.description: How the sides are chosen: Prefer (the listed ones) or SetRandom (drawn per instance).

enumDescriptions: The left edge.
The right edge.
The top edge (smaller y).
The bottom edge (larger y).
The middle of the grid. Only a pull (a ranking of the legal placements), never a hard rule, so it puts no condition on where the other components sit. Cannot be combined with other sides.

The bottom edge (larger y).
The middle of the grid. Only a pull (a ranking of the legal placements), never a hard rule, so it puts no condition on where the other components sit. Cannot be combined with other sides.

sides.description: Prefer only: one or two sides; two means a corner. Left with Right, or Top with Bottom, cancel out. Only used when `mode` is Prefer.

enumDescriptions: One of the four sides.
Two sides, one horizontal and one vertical: a random corner.
Left or Right.
Top or Bottom.
markdownEnumDescriptions: One of the four sides.
Two sides, one horizontal and one vertical: a random corner.
Left or Right.
Top or Bottom.

pick.description: SetRandom only: what is drawn. Default Any. Only used when `mode` is SetRandom.

weight.description: How strongly the pull counts against the arrangement's bias, when both are active (default 1; 0 turns it off).

SidePull.description: Pulls a shape towards a side or corner of the glyph. Among the shape's legal placements (the best-of-N candidates of its arrangement) the one nearest the chosen side(s) is kept. A ranking only: it never relaxes a hard rule, and the pull is as strong as arrangement.candidates is high.

enabled.description: Switches spacing on. While false the whole block is ignored, numbers included. Default false.

minCenterDistance.description: Minimum distance between the CENTROIDS of two shapes (the average of each shape's own node positions) - a coarse "keep this shape in its own area of the grid" check, independent of how close any individual pair of nodes gets. Only used when `enabled` is true.

minNodeDistance.description: Minimum distance between the CLOSEST pair of nodes belonging to two different shapes - a finer, local check that catches two shapes whose overall centers are far apart but which still reach out and nearly touch at one point. Only used when `enabled` is true.

maxNodeDistance.description: Maximum distance between the CLOSEST pair of nodes of the candidate and an existing shape. 0 = no maximum. Which existing shapes it must hold against is controlled by `maxDistanceMode`. Must be >= `minNodeDistance` when both are set. Only used when `enabled` is true.

minEdgeDistance.description: Minimum distance (lattice units) between the PATHS of this shape's strokes and every other stroke in the glyph (and between its own strokes), measured along the real curves - arcs, circles and bent lines included - not between nodes. Where two strokes meet on purpose (a shared node, an allowed crossing) the rule is waived within 1.5x this distance of the meeting point, so a stroke must leave a junction at an angle of roughly 40 degrees or more. Between two shapes the larger of their two values applies. 0 = off. In a combination (combination.arrangement.spacing) it is the clearance between the strokes of different components: a component's strokes keep this distance from those of the components placed before it, so components cannot lie on top of each other (a stroke of one component running along a stroke of another is too close). Needs enabled: true. A dot is a point and keeps this distance from other strokes too. Only used when `enabled` is true.

onlyShapes.description: Shape ids. When set, this shape's spacing rules (centroid, node and edge distance, maximum) are measured ONLY against the strokes drawn by these shapes; everything else is ignored by them. May name the shape itself (its own other instances). Not together with `excludeShapes`. The shape's own chain is always checked against itself. Shapes only. Only used when `enabled` is true. Not together with `excludeShapes`.

excludeShapes.description: Shape ids that this shape's spacing rules ignore (measured against everything else). Shapes only. Only used when `enabled` is true. Not together with `onlyShapes`.

enumDescriptions: Candidate must be within `maxNodeDistance` of AT LEAST ONE existing shape.
Candidate must be within `maxNodeDistance` of EVERY existing shape.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Candidate must be within `maxNodeDistance` of AT LEAST ONE existing shape.
Candidate must be within `maxNodeDistance` of EVERY existing shape.
maxDistanceMode.description: Only used when `maxNodeDistance` is above 0 (0 = no maximum). Only used when `enabled` is true.

ignoreStartNode.description: For a shape with placement.startOnExistingNode: leave the node it starts on out of the spacing checks (centroid, minimum and maximum node distance), since that node is shared with an existing shape and so sits at distance 0 from it. Every other node of the shape is still measured. Default false. Only used when `enabled` is true.

SpacingConfig.description: Spacing enforced between a shape and the shapes already placed, on top of (not instead of) the ordinary intersection check. Part of a shape's (or a combination's) arrangement rules; the spacing within one chain is `chain.selfSpacing`. Minimums keep things from sitting uncomfortably close together; maximums keep them clustered. Disabled by default, since these are additional constraints that can make placement noticeably harder to satisfy. A "shape" is one placed instance of a shapes entry when generating a glyph, and a whole placed component when combining glyphs per `combination.recipes` - both are checked the same way. The rules of the shape BEING PLACED are checked against EVERY already-placed shape (minimums against all; the maximum per `maxDistanceMode`), so the result depends on placement order.

shapes.description: Ids of the shapes that drew the strokes. Empty/missing = any shape.

A circle of diameter 0 only.
Part of a circle.
Any whole circle, a dot (a circle of diameter 0, as the Circle connection rule draws it) included.
A whole circle with a diameter above 0 (no dots).
A straight line.
A line with a bend.

kind.description: Only strokes of this form (Any, Dot, Arc, Circle, Ring, Line, Curve). Default Any.

glyphs.description: quality.pairRules only: the glyphs (by name, "*" = any glyph) whose strokes this selector picks from.

StrokeSelector.description: Picks strokes by the shape that drew them and by their form.

range.description: Used only when Options is empty.

options.description: Weighted ranges to pick from (for a bimodal look: mostly straight, sometimes strongly curved). Empty = use range.

TensionConfig.description: Bezier handle length as a fraction of the edge's length (capped at 0.5 downstream). Default behavior (Options empty) is a single continuous range, uniformly sampled - the same as a plain FloatRange used to be. Populating Options switches to a weighted pick among several ranges instead: this is what lets a language express an extreme/bimodal distribution like "70% dead straight (0-0), 30% strongly curved (0.4-0.5)" rather than one smooth spread across the whole range - a look a single continuous range can't produce, since it always fills in the middle values too. Not restricted to two options; any number of weighted bands works, following the same {value/range, weight} pattern as connection rules and scale ratios elsewhere in this schema.

min.description: Lowest tension of this band (a fraction of the edge length, at most 0.5).

max.description: Highest tension of this band. Must not be below min.

weight.description: How likely this band is relative to the others. Default 1.

TensionOption.description: One weighted tension range to pick from - see `tension`.

width.description: Width along the body of the stroke.

flareLength.description: Flare length as a fraction of each edge's length (capped at 0.5).

enumDescriptions: Width changes at a constant rate along the stroke.
Width eases in and out (smooth curve).
Width stays thin and widens sharply near the end.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Width changes at a constant rate along the stroke.

Width stays thin and widens sharply near the end.
profile.description: How the width changes along the flare: Linear, Smooth (default) or Sharp.

enumDescriptions: Only the two free ends of each chain.
Both ends of every edge.
Chain ends and every corner where two edges meet.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Only the two free ends of each chain.
Both ends of every edge.
Chain ends and every corner where two edges meet.

terminal.description: How the flared end is finished: Flat (default), Round or Ball.

ballScale.description: Ball diameter = `endWidth` * `ballScale` (Terminal == Ball only). Only used when `terminal` is Ball.

ThickEndsTypefaceConfig.description: Strokes of constant width whose ends flare wider (optionally ending in a ball).

perGlyphJitter.description: 0 = every glyph uses the identical typeface; 0.1 = each glyph's widths vary by up to +-10%.

TypefaceConfig.description: One typeface per language, resolved once from the seed (so every glyph in a language reads as the same font). Kind selects which sub-config is used; a null sub-config means defaults.

strength.description: Extra draws added per use. 0 = off. Positive: keep the lowest of the draws (smaller counts and lengths); negative: the same number of draws (its absolute value) but keep the highest (larger counts and lengths).

affectSubSymbolCount.description: Whether the bias is applied to the number of strokes (the shape's count). Default true.

affectSubSymbolLength.description: Whether the bias is applied to the chain length. Default true.

UsageSizeBiasConfig.description: Counteracts a size skew towards heavily-used component glyphs: the more recipes a plain glyph appears in, the more likely it is to roll LOW values for its sub-symbol count and sub-symbol lengths. (Components used rarely are the ones regenerated most while composites are being fitted, and what survives that is biased towards smaller, easier-to-place shapes - so the untouched, frequently-used ones end up bigger on average.) Mechanism: each use adds Strength "extra draws" - the glyph rolls its count/length that many extra times (the usual range, the usual rules) and keeps the lowest result. A NEGATIVE strength does the opposite: it rolls as many extra times as the same positive strength would, but keeps the HIGHEST result (-1 pushes frequently-used glyphs towards big, as 1 pushes them towards small). A fractional number of extra draws is honoured probabilistically. The result is always inside the configured min..max, so this only reshapes the odds; it never overrides a range or any other constraint. "Uses" = how many times the glyph's name appears across Combination.Recipes. A glyph used in no recipe is unaffected, as is everything when Strength is 0 (the default), in which case generation is bit-for-bit what it was. Rough feel, for a 3-value range (e.g. 1..3) and a glyph used twice: Strength 0.5 = 1 extra draw (lowest value ~55% of the time instead of 33%), Strength 1 = 2 extra draws (~70%). Guaranteed motifs have their own length range and are not affected.
